attributes.residual:
DEFICIT VERDICT, and it CORRECTS the lane assignment's framing. `--ops` line one reads `target-only: +2 lfsu +5 li / ours-only: -2 lfs -3 mr`, which invites reading the deficit as the li/mr family. THAT READING IS WRONG. Decomposing the 18 clusters by side gives target-only insns {addi@68, or@b0, or@c0, li@fac, li@1584, li@1688, addi@170c} = 7 and ours-only {or@a8, or@b8, mr@f9c, mr@1574, mr@1678} = 5; 7-5 = 2 = the deficit exactly. The three li/mr pairs are POSITIONALLY count-neutral (one ours-only mr against one target-only li each), and the two `or` are 2-on-2. So THE ENTIRE 2-INSTRUCTION DEFICIT IS THE TWO TARGET-ONLY `addi`, and neither the li/mr family nor the lfsu family can contribute to it.

CLUSTER 1 @170c (source-reachable candidate, now closed negative). Inner `dash` loop of the map_data byte-swap (src line 593-598, offsetof(map_data,dash)=8). Target: `li r5,0` then in-body `addi r10,r5,8` (materialise 8+acc) ; `add r10,r9,r10` ; `lfs f0,0(r10)` ; `addi r5,r5,4`. Ours: `add r9,r6,r10` then `lfs f0,8(r9)` - the +8 is folded into the load displacement, saving the addi. THREE distinct source spellings of the same addition were measured and ALL THREE returned NEUTRAL with byte-identical multiset 12t and real 1518: (a) named offset temp `o = offsetof(...) + j*4; WSWAPF(q,o);` (MWCC propagated the temp away entirely - nothing in the function changed), (b) operand-order swap `j*4 + offsetof(...)` per the rebase-operand-order law, (c) the statement-reorder probe on the sibling zero-init cluster. Two identical A/Bs on the reassociation axis kill it per the iteration rule: MWCC CANONICALISES `base + (const + induction)` into `(base + induction) + const` and folds const into the load displacement, and no source spelling of the addition reaches the choice. This is a NEW, NARROW, NAMED cap distinct from the offset-accumulator law, which governs WHERE induction updates are placed, not whether the constant term survives as its own addi.

CLUSTER 2 @68 (NOT source-reachable, and an S-CLASS SIGHTING WORTH THE CENSUS LANE'S ATTENTION). Target: `lis r3,@lbl_802576C0(HA)` ; `addi r4,r3,0 @LO` ; `add r3,r25,r0` ; `addi r22,r4,0` ; `lwz` ; `mr r3,r22` ; `bl MBSetupWad`. Ours: `lis r3,@HA` ; `add r4,r23,r0` ; `addi r3,r3,0 @LO` ; `lwz` ; `addi r26,r3,0` ; `bl`. The TARGET routes the ADDR16_LO completion through an extra volatile (r4) before homing to callee-saved r22, and OUR build does not - i.e. the target pays an address copy ours avoids. claim.law.addrlo-home-copy-class-is-general-temp-and-shadow-coupled.20260901.v1 FINDING 2 reports S (ours FEWER copies) = 0 over 953 opportunities image-wide. This site is at minimum an S-SHAPED SIGHTING inside a P-roster function and is flagged for that lane; it is not claimed as a refutation because the law's census counts a specific per-(function,callee-saved-register) shape-B statistic that this one aligned window does not by itself recompute. Closing it would require ADDING an instruction, so it is not source-reachable in the ordinary direction.

STILL OPEN AND NOT PROBED THIS PASS (the honest remainder, real 1518): the two lfsu rows @c60 and @1ab0 (count-neutral but real-visible; live lever = claim.law.block-scope-cursor-restores-lwzu-where-mutation-sinks.20260831.v1, untried here), the three li/mr zero-init pairs (count-neutral; ONE statement-reorder spelling measured NEUTRAL, the population is 3 and a respell of the remaining two is untried), and the two `or` position swaps. This function is nowhere near exact and the deficit verdict does not change that; what the pass establishes is that the DEFICIT specifically is the two addi, so no future pass should spend probes on the li/mr or lfsu families expecting the count to close.
